verdict.rationale: Sill is a remote-desktop tool, and remote-access products commonly offer shared address books and group policies, so this axis applies. The evidence shows only a per-Mac list of paired devices, which you can remove one by one. Sill also states there is "no account and no server," so it has no shared console, no user or machine grouping, and no per-group access policies.

support.subject: As an IT admin, machines and users are organized in a shared address book or console with per-group access policies
